newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says to earn $6 bln from tourism in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says to earn $6 bln from tourism in 1996.

text.p: Indonesia said on Monday it expected to earn $6 billion from foreign tourists in 1996, an increase of 18 percent from the previous year.

"We expect to earn around $6 billion this year from an expected five million tourist arrivals," Tourism, Post and Telecommunications Minister Joop Ave told reporters during a year-end press conference.
"We expect the fifth million tourist to arrive at Menado's Sam Ratulangi Airport in North Sulawesi later today," Ave said.
Indonesia had predicted it would receive between 4.78 and 5.05 million tourist arrivals this year.
Ave said Indonesia expected to increase the number of foreign tourist arrivals to around 6.5 million in 1997, but he gave no details on expected revenues.

Economist Dorodjatun Kuntjorojakti, a tourism industry analyst, said during the news conference that foreign tourists stayed an average 12 days in Indonesia, which was among the highest in the region.
Ave said the tourism sector was the country's third biggest foreign exchange earner after the oil and gas sector and the textile industry.
He added that the tourism sector employed some five million people, or 5.5 percent of the country's total workforce.
